extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, individuals, groups, nonprofits, lobbying organizations, and representatives who want to submit comments to U.S. federal agencies
extracted.subtask_short: submitting public comments to federal agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for drafting, formatting, submitting, and tracking public comments on proposed federal rules and regulations (U.S. rulemaking). Covers who may submit, timelines, submission methods, content tips, file requirements, and tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is a public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: A public comment is feedback submitted to a federal agency regarding proposed rules or regulations. The Administrative Procedures Act of 1946 requires agencies to keep the public informed and allows citizens to participate in rule-making beyond voting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the purpose and legal basis for submitting comments (participation in rulemaking under the APA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can submit
rubrics_metrics.description: "Any person, groups, organizations — including non-profit organizations and lobbying groups — or other federal agency" may submit comments, anonymously or through a representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone may submit, including organizations and other agencies; submissions may be anonymous or made via a representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: 60-day comment period follows publication (closes 7:00 PM ET for written, 11:59 PM ET for digital submissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the official comment period length and the differing closing times for written vs. digital submissions; plan to submit before these deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency reply obligation / how comments are handled
rubrics_metrics.description: 30-day reply period follows, during which agencies must respond to comments. Agencies must address all public comments in final regulations, explaining whether each was incorporated or out of scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are required to consider and respond to comments in their final rulemaking materials; this explains how comments are used and why specific, on-point input matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit — Regulations.gov procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Visit www.regulations.gov, search your docket, click "Comment," and submit feedback with up to 20 files (10MB each max).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Regulations.gov as the primary portal: locate docket by ID, follow the site workflow to attach files (observe per-file limits) and submit your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit — Agency websites
rubrics_metrics.description: Navigate to specific agency sites for comment portals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some agencies host their own comment portals or provide links; follow the instructions on the agency's site if provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit — Mail
rubrics_metrics.description: Send to addresses listed in Federal Register notices; must be postmarked by deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting by mail, use the address provided in the Federal Register notice and ensure the mailing is postmarked on or before the deadline to be considered timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit — Public hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver comments in-person at scheduled hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may hold public hearings where you can present comments orally or deliver written materials; follow the hearing schedule and procedures announced in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the docket ID number in your heading
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the docket ID number in your heading (e.g., "FDA-2017-D-6580-4894").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the official docket ID in your comment heading ensures your submission is correctly associated with the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the regulation thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.description: Know the regulation thoroughly before commenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the proposed rule and supporting materials completely so your comment addresses actual regulatory text, rationale, and specific provisions rather than generalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish your expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish your expertise with relevant credentials or experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide your qualifications, professional experience, or organizational affiliation to lend credibility to technical or factual assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be clear and organized
rubrics_metrics.description: Be clear and organized: define objectives, use precise language, present data-supported arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure comments with a clear statement of objectives, use concise and precise wording, and support positions with data or documented evidence to improve persuasiveness and agency uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite sources when referencing outside materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full citations or links to studies, data, statutes, or prior comments you rely on so reviewers can verify and incorporate your evidence into the administrative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address specific questions in the proposed rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Address specific questions posed within the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond directly to the questions and request-for-comments items listed in the notice to make your input actionable for the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: File submission details (acceptable file types and size limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Valid file types include: .pdf, .docx, .xlsx, .txt, .jpg, .png, and several others. Each file cannot exceed 10MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attaching supporting documents, use accepted file formats and keep each attachment at or below the stated 10MB per-file limit; Regulations.gov additionally permits up to 20 files per submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking your comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use "find a comment" at https://www.regulations.gov/help to locate submitted comments using your confirmation number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission, record your confirmation number and use Regulations.gov's tools to verify the comment appears in the docket and to track any public posting or agency responses.
